is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles funestus vectors in Uganda (page 3, 7).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc-995F, Vgsc-995S, Vgsc-1570Y, Cyp6aap-Dup1, Cyp6p4-236M, ZZB-TE, Cyp4j5-43F, Coeae1d, and 2La (page 7, 10).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Supplementary Figure 1 (page 30) provides genotype counts (N) for Vgsc-995, Cyp6p4-236M, Coeae1d, Cyp4j5-43F, and 2La inversion.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from 48 districts in Uganda (page 3, 7).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study reporting on the LLINEUP trial entomological surveillance (page 3, 8).

sub_country_location.evidence: Data is reported by health sub-districts (HSDs) across 48 districts in Uganda (page 7, 26).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted over a 2-year follow-up period from 2017-2019 (page 3, 12).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The paper states that while abundance data were reported previously, the molecular data from the 6, 12, 18, and 25-month collection rounds are novel to this manuscript (page 8).

supplement.evidence: The necessary genotype counts are provided in Supplementary Figure 1 on page 30 of the provided document.

assessment.summary: This study analyzed the frequency of insecticide resistance markers in Anopheles gambiae s.s. collected across 48 districts in Uganda during a 2-year cluster-randomized trial of PBO-LLINs versus conventional LLINs. The study found significant increases in several resistance markers over time, with Vgsc-995F spreading and replacing Vgsc-995S.
